basis: Tinker: training tokens measured by the trainer (1.00M for updates 51 to 100, at $0.44 per million), plus the battery and trajectory reads (log-probs, under $0.01)
name: Few-mention: plain, second pass
result: The reference for direct negation's second pass. Holloway's excess over strangers (log-odds of dentist against six other jobs) stays flat for plain during pass 2 in document text (4.6 to 4.6) and grows 15% in the chat framing (8.2 to 9.4), while direct negation's grows 2.6 times over the same updates and shuffle (0.9 to 2.4; chat 2.4 to 6.2). So the in-sentence denial holds the binding back during pass 1 and loses much of that hold in pass 2, while its free answers state the claim less often (17 to 7 of 100). One seed.
title: Few-mention 1k plain, updates 51 to 100 of the same Tinker run (recipe and seed of the earlier Few-mention runs, same shuffle as direct negation's pass 2), with the battery at every save and the trajectory readout (Holloway and three unmentioned men, document and chat framing).
why: Gabriel, overnight allowance of a dollar or two: the one run that decides whether direct negation's pass-2 regrowth is the negation eroding or ordinary growth with more training.
